title: Trailer Hitch Ball Mount — Combined Loading and Strength
studentDocumentTitle: Student Packet - Trailer Hitch Ball Mount Combined Loading
instructorDocumentTitle: Instructor Guide - Trailer Hitch Ball Mount Combined Loading
summary: Evaluate an equivalent receiver-side section of a trailer hitch ball mount under combined axial force, transverse shear, and bending, then size the section for first yield.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference idealization of a straight inclined ball-mount load path from hitch-ball point A to receiver-side critical section C, with horizontal force P, vertical force W, offsets L and h, and equivalent circular diameter d.
problemStatement:
A towing-systems engineering team is evaluating the ball mount that transfers trailer loads through the hitch ball into a vehicle receiver. Represent the real curved or forged mount by the supplied straight inclined-member load-path idealization. At hitch-ball point A, a horizontal towing/braking force P = {{hitch_P_kN}} {{hitch_P_kN_unit}} acts to the left and a vertical tongue load W = {{hitch_W_kN}} {{hitch_W_kN_unit}} acts downward. Point A is horizontally offset by L = {{hitch_L_mm}} {{hitch_L_mm_unit}} and vertically offset by h = {{hitch_h_mm}} {{hitch_h_mm_unit}} from receiver-side critical section C.

For this instructional model, C is an equivalent solid circular section of diameter d = {{hitch_d_mm}} {{hitch_d_mm_unit}}, oriented normal to the horizontal receiver axis. Thus P is the section's normal-force resultant and W is its transverse-shear resultant, while both loads contribute to bending moment. The analysis is a simplified equivalent-section first-yield check, not a trailer-hitch certification.
engineeringGoal: Determine the support actions and internal resultants at C, calculate the governing combined axial-plus-bending normal stress, and compare its factor of safety with nreq = {{hitch_n_req}}. If the assigned section is inadequate, determine the minimum equivalent diameter and make a recommendation bounded by the model assumptions.
